---
title: "Cross-Compilation of Packages"
---

# Cross-Compilation of Packages

When building an entire distribution from scratch, you have two choices:
1. **Native Chroot Compilation:** Compile software inside an emulated or native container using the target CPU architecture. (Slow if building ARM64 on x86 via QEMU user emulation).
2. **True Cross-Compilation:** Run cross-compilers (`aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc`) natively on high-powered x86_64 host hardware to emit target machine code directly.

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|              Cross-Compilation Package Setup                |
|                                                             |
|  Host System (x86_64):                                      |
|  - Cross Compiler: aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc                    |
|  - Target Sysroot: /opt/sysroots/aarch64                    |
|       ├── usr/include (target C headers)                    |
|       └── usr/lib     (target shared libraries)             |
|                                                             |
|  pkg-config Configuration:                                  |
|  - PKG_CONFIG_SYSROOT_DIR=/opt/sysroots/aarch64             |
|  - PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR=/opt/sysroots/aarch64/usr/lib/pkgconfig|
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## The Pitfall: `pkg-config` Poisoning

When building packages that depend on external libraries (e.g., compiling `curl` which depends on `openssl`), the build system invokes `pkg-config` to discover library paths and CFLAGS:

```bash
$ pkg-config --cflags --libs openssl
-I/usr/include -L/usr/lib -lssl -lcrypto # DANGER: Points to host libraries!
```

If your build system uses the host's `/usr/bin/pkg-config`, it will return the host machine's library paths! The linker will link against host x86_64 binaries, causing immediate cross-compilation linker errors.

### The Solution: Cross-`pkg-config` Wrappers
Create an architecture-specific wrapper script at `$TOOLS/bin/aarch64-linux-gnu-pkg-config`:

```bash
#!/bin/sh
# aarch64-linux-gnu-pkg-config
export PKG_CONFIG_SYSROOT_DIR="/opt/sysroots/aarch64"
export PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR="/opt/sysroots/aarch64/usr/lib/pkgconfig:/opt/sysroots/aarch64/usr/share/pkgconfig"
export PKG_CONFIG_SYSTEM_INCLUDE_PATH="/opt/sysroots/aarch64/usr/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_SYSTEM_LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/sysroots/aarch64/usr/lib"

exec /usr/bin/pkg-config "$@"
```

## Cross-Compiling with Meson Cross-Files

Meson provides first-class support for cross-compilation via declarative INI files:

```ini
# /opt/cross/aarch64-linux.ini
[binaries]
c = 'aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc'
cpp = 'aarch64-linux-gnu-g++'
ar = 'aarch64-linux-gnu-ar'
strip = 'aarch64-linux-gnu-strip'
pkg-config = 'aarch64-linux-gnu-pkg-config'

[host_machine]
system = 'linux'
cpu_family = 'aarch64'
cpu = 'cortex-a72'
endian = 'little'

[properties]
sys_root = '/opt/sysroots/aarch64'
```

Invoking the build requires a single flag:
```bash
$ meson setup build --cross-file /opt/cross/aarch64-linux.ini
$ ninja -C build
```
The resulting binaries are guaranteed to run natively on the target architecture without host pollution.
